first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence directly links shorter onboarding and reduced signup friction to faster time-to-value and first-week activation. A guarded simplification test is the most direct route to durable qualified revenue while avoiding an unvalidated broad price response. Verify the onboarding result and the pricing result because their comparative long-term revenue implications are consequential.

final.rationale: Run a standard controlled onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation, while verified evidence shows shortened onboarding increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%. Promotional pricing is not suitable for the long-term qualified-revenue objective: although it raised signup and short-term qualified revenue, the discounted cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention. Monitor qualification, retention, and revenue quality alongside completion and activation before any broader rollout.
